history.dynasty: Guhila (Guhilot) of Mewar - built under Rawal Allata
history.period: 10th century CE; earliest inscription dated 961 AD records a repair, implying an older shrine (possibly 7th century per archaeological records - verify)
history.summary: CSV town 'Udaipur' corrected: the temple stands in Jagat village, about 50 km southeast of Udaipur city in a cleft of the Aravalli hills (Jagat is in Udaipur district). One of Rajasthan's finest 10th-century shrines, built under Guhila king Rawal Allata; the earliest surviving inscription (961 AD) records a repair, suggesting an earlier shrine existed here. An early transitional example of Maru-Gurjara architecture, famous for its exquisitely preserved exterior carvings - earning it the nickname 'Khajuraho of Rajasthan/Mewar' - depicting deities, musicians, dancers and courtesans; the pentagonal shrine has 17 turrets and a pagoda-like gabled roof behind a massive rampart wall. Legend connects it to Jainism: Ambika is said to have appeared in a dream to Vimala Shah, guiding him to build the Adinath temple at Mount Abu (a local legend, not documented history). Protected by the State Department of Archaeology and Museum, Rajasthan. Coordinates below are published coordinates from Wikipedia (24.291167, 73.845333); the exact shrine position in the rock cleft is unverified (verify).

name: Ambika Mata Temple
town_description: Jagat is a small village in Udaipur district, Rajasthan, about 50 km southeast of Udaipur city in the Aravalli hills. It is known almost entirely for the 10th-century Ambika Mata temple - a non-commercial, low-crowd heritage site with free entry and ASI signage only.
